FEATURES.spot: Has the Great Red Spot — a giant storm
FEATURES.olympus: Has the tallest mountain — Olympus Mons
FEATURES.morning: It is called the Morning Star
FEATURES.icy: An icy giant, turquoise in color
FEATURES.math: It was found thanks to math
FEATURES.moons: Has two tiny moons — Phobos and Deimos
FEATURES.titan: Has the moon Titan, with an atmosphere of its own

0.1: Cassiopeia looks like the letter W. It is named after a queen from a myth.

1.1: The Southern Cross can be seen only from the southern half of the Earth — it is on the flag of Australia.

2.1: Sagitta means “the Arrow”. It is one of the smallest constellations in the sky.

3.1: Delphinus, the Dolphin, is small but easy to spot in the summer sky.

4.1: Aries is the ram with the golden fleece from an ancient Greek myth.

5.1: The four bright stars of Corvus, the Crow, make a four-sided shape in the sky.

6.1: The Big Dipper is seven stars of the Great Bear constellation. It looks like a ladle.

7.1: At the tip of the Little Bear’s “tail” shines the North Star — it always points north.

8.1: The constellation Cepheus looks like a little house with a pointed roof.

9.1: In Lyra, the Harp, shines Vega — one of the brightest stars in our sky.

10.1: The two brightest stars of Gemini, the Twins, are called Castor and Pollux — like the brothers in the myth.

11.1: The stars of the Northern Crown form a half circle — just like a real crown.

12.1: In the heart of Scorpius, the Scorpion, burns the red star Antares.

13.1: Draco, the Dragon, winds its way between the Great Bear and the Little Bear.

14.1: Orion is the hunter of the sky. The three stars in the middle are his belt.

15.1: The brightest star of Leo, the Lion, is called Regulus — “the little king”.

16.1: Hydra is the longest constellation in the whole sky.

0.0: Which planet goes around the Sun the fastest?
0.1: Mercury races around the Sun faster than any other planet — almost 50 kilometers every second.

1.0: On which planet is it over 400 degrees by day and minus 170 by night?
1.1: Mercury has almost no air to hold the warmth: by day it scorches, and by night there is a bitter frost.

2.0: Which planet is only a little bigger than our Moon?
2.1: Mercury is only a little bigger than the Moon — and covered with craters just the same.

3.0: Which planet is all craters and looks very much like the Moon?
3.1: The surface of Mercury is pitted with craters: meteorites have been hitting it for billions of years.

4.0: Which planet has neither moons nor air?
4.1: Mercury has no moon at all and almost no atmosphere.

5.0: Which planet does sunlight reach the soonest — in just three minutes?
5.1: Light from the Sun takes about three minutes to reach Mercury, and more than eight to reach the Earth.

6.0: On which planet does the Sun look three times bigger in the sky than from the Earth?
6.1: From Mercury the Sun looks three times bigger than from the Earth — that is how close it is.

7.0: Which planet is named after the swift Roman messenger god?
7.1: Mercury was the Romans’ messenger god in winged sandals. The planet got his name because it is the fastest.

8.0: Which planet is the hardest to see from the Earth, because it hides in the glare of the Sun?
8.1: Mercury can be seen only for a short while at dawn or just after sunset — it always stays close to the Sun.

9.0: Which planet did the spacecraft MESSENGER work at?
9.1: The MESSENGER spacecraft circled Mercury for four years and photographed its whole surface.

10.0: On which planet is ice hidden in dark craters near the poles, although it is the nearest to the Sun?
10.1: The Sun never looks into the craters at Mercury’s poles, so ice lies there.

11.0: In which planet does an iron core take up almost the whole inside?
11.1: Mercury is like an iron ball in a thin stone shell: the core takes up most of it.

0.0: On which planet is it 460 degrees both by day and by night?
0.1: Venus is hotter than an oven: its thick clouds do not let the heat out by day or by night.

1.0: Which planet is wrapped in thick yellow clouds of acid?
1.1: The clouds of Venus are made of burning acid. The surface of the planet cannot be seen through them.

2.0: Which planet is called the Earth’s sister, because it is almost the same size?
2.1: Venus is almost the same size as the Earth, but nothing could live on it.

3.0: On which planet does the Sun rise in the west and set in the east?
3.1: Venus spins backwards, so the Sun rises there in the west.

4.0: Which planet turns the slowest — once in 243 Earth days?
4.1: Venus turns so slowly that one turn takes longer than its year.

5.0: Which planet is the brightest in our night sky?
5.1: After the Sun and the Moon, the brightest thing in the sky is Venus: its clouds reflect light wonderfully.

6.0: On which planet does the air press as hard as if you were at the bottom of an ocean?
6.1: The air on Venus presses ninety times harder than on the Earth — like water a kilometer deep.

7.0: Which planet is named after the Roman goddess of beauty?
7.1: Venus was the Roman goddess of beauty and love. The planet got her name for its bright glow.

8.0: Which planet has the most volcanoes?
8.1: Venus has more than a thousand big volcanoes — more than any other planet.

9.0: Which planet comes the closest to the Earth?
9.1: Venus comes closer to the Earth than any other planet — but even then it is forty million kilometers away.

10.0: Which planet is the second from the Sun?
10.1: Venus is the second planet from the Sun, between Mercury and the Earth.

11.0: On which planet does acid rain fall and dry up before it reaches the ground?
11.1: It is so hot on Venus that drops of acid rain turn to vapor while still in the air.

0.0: On which planet is there liquid water — rivers, seas and oceans?
0.1: Only on the Earth does water flow in rivers and fill oceans: it is neither too hot nor too cold here.

1.0: Which is the only planet where there is life for certain?
1.1: The Earth is the only planet we know that has life: plants, animals and people.

2.0: On which planet does a day last exactly 24 hours?
2.1: The Earth turns around once in 24 hours — that is why day follows night.

3.0: On which planet does a year last 365 days?
3.1: In 365 days the Earth goes once around the Sun — and that is a year.

4.0: Which planet is the third from the Sun?
4.1: The Earth is the third planet from the Sun, between Venus and Mars.

5.0: On which planet is there air that people can breathe?
5.1: Only the air of the Earth has enough oxygen for people and animals to breathe.

6.0: Which planet looks blue from space, with white clouds and green continents?
6.1: From space the Earth looks like a little blue ball: most of it is covered with water.

7.0: Which planet does light from the Sun reach in a little over eight minutes?
7.1: A ray of sunlight reaches the Earth in eight minutes and twenty seconds.

8.0: Which planet is the biggest of the four rocky ones?
8.1: The Earth is the biggest of the rocky planets: bigger than Venus, Mars and Mercury.

9.0: Which planet does the International Space Station fly around?
9.1: The International Space Station goes around the Earth in an hour and a half.

10.0: Which planet did all the space rockets take off from?
10.1: Every rocket, satellite and astronaut set out for space from the Earth.

11.0: On which planet do you weigh exactly what the scales at home show?
11.1: The scales at home show your weight on the Earth. On other planets it would be different.

12.0: On which planet is there a total eclipse of the Sun, when the Moon covers the Sun exactly?
12.1: From the Earth the Moon and the Sun look the same size, so the Moon can cover the Sun completely.

0.0: Which planet do rovers drive across?
0.1: Robot rovers drive across Mars: they take pictures, drill into rocks and look for traces of water.

1.0: On which planet is the daytime sky pinkish-red and the sunset blue?
1.1: Because of the rusty dust, the sky on Mars is pink by day and blue at sunset. On the Earth it is the other way around.

2.0: Which planet has the biggest canyon in the Solar System?
2.1: Valles Marineris on Mars is so long that it would stretch right across Europe.

3.0: On which planet is a day only a little longer than ours — 24 hours 37 minutes?
3.1: A day on Mars is almost the same as on the Earth: only thirty-seven minutes longer.

4.0: On which planet does a year last almost two Earth years?
4.1: Mars goes around the Sun in 687 days — almost two Earth years.

5.0: On which planet do people dream of building the first base?
5.1: Scientists are preparing to send people to Mars: of all the planets it is the most like the Earth.

6.0: On which planet can dust storms cover the whole of it?
6.1: A dust storm on Mars can cover the whole planet with dust for several months.

7.0: Which planet has ice caps at its poles and the dry beds of ancient rivers?
7.1: Rivers once flowed on Mars. Now water is left there only as ice.

8.0: Which planet is named after the Roman god of war?
8.1: Mars was the Roman god of war. The planet got his name for its red color.

9.0: Which planet is the fourth from the Sun?
9.1: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun, right after the Earth.

10.0: Which planet is about half as wide as the Earth?
10.1: Mars is half as wide as the Earth — and ten times lighter.

11.0: On which planet did a helicopter from the Earth fly for the first time?
11.1: The little helicopter Ingenuity took off on Mars — the first flight ever on another planet.

12.0: On which planet was ice found under the soil, and where do we look for traces of ancient life?
12.1: There is ice under the soil of Mars. Scientists are looking to see whether microbes once lived there.

0.0: On which planet would you weigh the most — two and a half times more than on the Earth?
0.1: Jupiter pulls the hardest: a child who weighs thirty kilograms would weigh seventy-five there.

1.1: Jupiter turns around once in under ten hours — faster than any other planet.

2.0: Which planet is the fifth from the Sun — the first of the giants?
2.1: Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun and the first of the four giants.

3.0: Which planet is heavier than all the other planets put together?
3.1: Jupiter is two and a half times heavier than all the other planets together.

4.0: Which planet has the moon Europa, with an ocean under its ice?
4.1: Under the icy crust of Europa, a moon of Jupiter, hides an ocean of salty water.

5.0: Which planet has the moon Io, with hundreds of active volcanoes?
5.1: Io, a moon of Jupiter, is the most volcanic place in the Solar System.

6.0: Galileo discovered four big moons of which planet?
6.1: Through his telescope Galileo saw four moons of Jupiter: Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto.

7.0: On which planet does a year last almost twelve Earth years?
7.1: Jupiter goes around the Sun in almost twelve Earth years.

8.0: Which planet is striped — with brown and white belts of cloud?
8.1: The stripes of Jupiter are belts of cloud that the wind drives in different directions.

9.0: Which planet is named after the chief Roman god?
9.1: Jupiter was the king of the Roman gods. The biggest planet was given his name.

10.0: Which planet does the spacecraft Juno work at?
10.1: The Juno spacecraft circles Jupiter and peers beneath its clouds.

11.0: Which planet protects the Earth by pulling comets and asteroids toward itself?
11.1: With its pull Jupiter catches many comets and asteroids that might otherwise fly toward the Earth.

12.0: On which planet do the most powerful auroras shine?
12.1: The auroras on Jupiter are hundreds of times more powerful than those on the Earth, and they never go out.

0.0: Which planet has the most moons — more than a hundred and forty?
0.1: More than a hundred and forty moons have been found around Saturn — more than around any other planet.

1.0: Which planet is the second biggest?
1.1: Saturn is the second biggest planet: only Jupiter is bigger.

2.0: Which planet is the sixth from the Sun?
2.1: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun, between Jupiter and Uranus.

3.0: On which planet does a year last almost thirty Earth years?
3.1: Saturn goes around the Sun in twenty-nine and a half Earth years.

4.0: The rings of which planet are made of pieces of ice and rock?
4.1: The rings of Saturn are billions of bits of ice and stone: from the size of a grain of sand to the size of a house.

5.0: At the pole of which planet does an amazing six-sided storm spin?
5.1: At the north pole of Saturn rages a storm in the shape of a perfect hexagon.

6.0: Which planet has the moon Enceladus, which shoots fountains of water into space?
6.1: Enceladus, a moon of Saturn, shoots geysers into space from under its icy crust.

7.0: Which planet did the Cassini spacecraft study for thirteen years?
7.1: The Cassini spacecraft spent thirteen years studying Saturn, its rings and its moons.

8.0: Which planet is named after the Roman god of farming and time?
8.1: Saturn was the Romans’ god of farming and time, the father of Jupiter.

9.0: Which planet is the farthest of those easily seen without a telescope?
9.1: Saturn is the farthest planet that people have always been able to see with the naked eye.

10.0: Which planet is the most squashed — like a flattened ball?
10.1: Saturn spins so fast that it has visibly flattened at the poles.

11.0: The rings of which planet can be seen even through a small telescope?
11.1: The rings of Saturn are so wide and bright that they can be seen even through an amateur telescope.

12.0: On a moon of which planet are there lakes and rain of liquid gas?
12.1: On Titan, a moon of Saturn, there are lakes and rivers — not of water, but of liquid methane.

0.0: Which planet is the coldest — it gets down to minus 224 degrees there?
0.1: The lowest temperature of any planet was measured on Uranus: minus 224 degrees.

1.0: Which planet is the seventh from the Sun?
1.1: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun, between Saturn and Neptune.

2.0: On which planet does a year last 84 Earth years?
2.1: Uranus goes around the Sun in eighty-four Earth years — as long as a long human life.

3.0: On which planet do winter and summer last twenty-one years each?
3.1: Uranus lies on its side, so each season there lasts twenty-one years.

4.0: Which planet was the first to be discovered with a telescope?
4.1: Uranus was the first planet discovered through a telescope — by William Herschel.

5.0: The moons of which planet are named after characters from Shakespeare?
5.1: The moons of Uranus are named like characters in Shakespeare’s plays: Titania, Oberon, Miranda, Ariel.

6.0: Which planet is named after the Greek god of the sky?
6.1: Uranus was the ancient Greek god of the sky. It is the only planet with a Greek name rather than a Roman one.

7.0: Which planet does sunlight take almost three hours to reach?
7.1: A ray of sunlight takes two hours and forty minutes to reach Uranus.

8.0: Which planet is the third biggest?
8.1: Uranus is the third biggest planet, after Jupiter and Saturn.

9.0: On which planet can a pole be lit by the Sun for forty-two years in a row?
9.1: At the poles of Uranus a day lasts forty-two years, and then a night lasts just as long.

10.0: Which planet rolls along its orbit on its side, like a ball, and has thirteen dark rings?
10.1: Uranus has thirteen thin dark rings, and they stand almost upright, because the planet lies on its side.

0.0: Which planet is the eighth — the last — from the Sun?
0.1: Neptune is the eighth and last planet of the Solar System.

1.0: On which planet does a year last 165 Earth years?
1.1: Neptune goes around the Sun in one hundred sixty-five Earth years.

2.0: Which planet does sunlight take more than four hours to reach?
2.1: A ray of sunlight takes four hours and ten minutes to reach Neptune.

3.0: Which planet is dark blue, like the deep sea?
3.1: Neptune is dark blue: the methane gas in its air soaks up red light.

4.0: Which planet is named after the Roman god of the seas?
4.1: Neptune was the Roman god of the seas. The blue planet was given his name.

5.0: Which planet has the moon Triton, which circles it “backwards”?
5.1: Triton, a moon of Neptune, goes around the opposite way — not the way the planet itself turns.

6.0: Which planet can never be seen without a telescope — even on the darkest night?
6.1: Neptune is so far away that it can be seen only through a telescope.

7.0: On which planet has only one year passed since the day it was discovered?
7.1: Neptune was discovered in 1846, and it finished its first full trip around the Sun only in 2011.

8.0: Which planet is the fourth biggest, but heavier than Uranus?
8.1: Neptune is a little narrower than Uranus, yet heavier.

9.0: Which planet is the farthest from the Earth?
9.1: Neptune is the planet farthest from us: more than four billion kilometers away.

10.0: On which planet was the Great Dark Spot seen — a storm as big as the Earth?
10.1: The Great Dark Spot on Neptune is a gigantic storm. It disappears and then comes back again.

11.0: Which planet did Voyager 2 fly past last, before leaving the Solar System?
11.1: Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft ever to visit Neptune. After that it flew off toward the stars.

12.0: On which planet do the seasons last forty years each?
12.1: A year on Neptune is so long that each season there lasts more than forty Earth years.

planets.label: Parade of Planets
planets.blurb: Line up the planets from the Sun and by size, and learn a hundred curious things about them
planets.intro: Eight planets circle the Sun. Line them up in order: first the one nearest the Sun!

constellations.label: Space Navigator
constellations.blurb: Join the stars in order, draw constellations and find them in the starry sky
constellations.intro: In the sky the stars make pictures — constellations. Tap the stars in order, starting from the smallest number, and see what comes out!

planets.1: Now the far-off giant planets: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
planets.2: Planets can be tiny or gigantic. Line them up by size: from the smallest to the biggest!
planets.3: Every planet is special in some way. Match each clue to the planet it tells about.
planets.4: Now — questions about the planets: where it is hot and where it is cold, where there is water, how long a day and a year last. Tap the planet in question!

constellations.1: Now the counting does not start from one. Find the smallest number and go on in order.
constellations.2: The constellations are getting bigger, and now the stars carry letters. Join them in alphabetical order!
constellations.3: Now we count in twos: two, four, six, eight…
constellations.4: And now in tens: ten, twenty, thirty…
constellations.5: Now there are many stars in the sky, and they have no numbers. The stars of the constellation are a little bigger than the others. Find them and join them with your finger!
constellations.6: There are more stars in the sky now, and the constellation’s stars are not so big any more. Look closely!
constellations.7: The hardest sky: the stars of the constellation are only slightly bigger than the others.

size.fact: From the smallest to the biggest: {names}.
